You are building a numerical PARITY BATTERY for the treams-rs package (repo at treams-rs, a T-matrix electromagnetic scattering library: Rust core + PyO3 extension + Python API treams_rs). Several engineers are about to refactor and optimize the Rust core, bindings and Python layer in separate git worktrees. The user requires that numerical results stay the same within tight floating-point tolerance (not necessarily bit-identical). Your battery is the global safety net that proves this.

Deliverable (OUTSIDE the repository — do not modify anything under treams-rs):

  1. battery.py — a single self-contained script with two modes:
    • python battery.py record OUT.npz evaluates every case and saves all outputs.
    • python battery.py compare REF.npz [--rtol 1e-10] [--atol-scale 1e-13] [--only PATTERN] re-evaluates and compares against REF, printing a table of per-case max relative error (relative to the case's max magnitude), and exits nonzero if any case exceeds tolerance, a case disappears, or a case newly raises. Cases that raise an exception in record mode are recorded as such (exception type + message) and must raise the same exception type in compare mode. Each case is a named function returning a dict of numpy arrays (complex/real/int). Use fixed seeds (numpy default_rng with per-case seeds); no dependence on thread count or dict ordering. Keep each case fast (the whole battery should run in under ~90 s on the debug extension with 4 CPUs).
  2. baseline.npz recorded from the CURRENT build (the debug extension already installed in .venv, importing from python).
  3. README.md — how to run it from a worktree: cd <worktree> && PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python .venv/bin/python battery.py compare baseline.npz, plus the list of cases.

Coverage — aim for BROAD coverage of every public numerical entry point, forward values AND analytic pullbacks (use random complex cotangents with fixed seeds and call context.pullback(cotangent); record every gradient array returned). Discover the surface from: treams_rs.support_catalog() / python -m treams_rs --format json, docs/api.md, docs/user-guide.md, python/treams_rs/_native.pyi, python/treams_rs/diff.py, and the tests in tests (they show valid inputs for every function). Include at least:

  • special functions (spherical/cylindrical Bessel, Hankel, derivatives, Legendre incl. fractional degree, pi/tau, spherical harmonics, Wigner 3j at small and LARGE j (e.g. j up to 60-100 with extreme m, since a known instability there is about to be fixed — put these in separately named cases wigner3j_large_* so an expected change can be isolated), Wigner small-d / full D, incomplete gamma incl. negative degrees and large |z|, Kambe integrals) with broadcasting;
  • vector spherical/cylindrical/plane waves, coordinate transforms, translations (regular/outgoing, spherical/cylindrical/polar), rotations, expansions/conversions between bases, periodic conversion;
  • sphere/multilayer/chiral sphere and cylinder T-matrices, EBCM (corrected and legacy), T-matrix metrics (CD, duality breaking, chirality), cross sections;
  • clusters: particle_cluster, cluster solves (full/requested/factor reuse), matrix-free iterative SphereCluster, interaction solves, the requested-illumination paths;
  • fields: efield/hfield/dfield/bfield-style families on scattered and incident waves, field operators, weighted samples, both spherical and cylindrical bases, samples near the polar axis and near origins;
  • lattice sums (1D/2D/3D spherical, 1D/2D cylindrical, full/real/reciprocal/shells), periodic coupling/solve_periodic, channels, diffraction orders;
  • planar: interfaces (chiral Fresnel), propagation, slabs, stacks, S-matrix composition/doubling, power (transmission/reflection/absorption), circular dichroism, bands, internal illumination (smatrix_illuminate), transmittance;
  • linear algebra helpers exposed publicly (linear_solve, svd values, eig) and their pullbacks;
  • high-level physics-object workflows from the user guide (sphere.scatter, Cluster.scatter/solve/factor, solve_periodic → to_smatrix → stack → power, fields on scattered waves). Where a function has both a diff.* recorded version and a plain version, record both. Prefer moderately sized inputs (lmax 2-6, a few particles, tens to hundreds of points) plus a few larger ones for the hot paths (e.g. scattered-field evaluation with 16 spheres lmax 4 at ~500 points; a cluster translation-table-heavy case at lmax 8).

Tolerance design: compare with |new - ref| <= rtol * max(|ref|) per array plus a small absolute floor; report per-case max errors so reviewers can see near-misses. Make it robust to ordering (always return arrays in a deterministic order). Validate the battery: record baseline, then run compare against it twice (must pass with ~0 error), and run a deliberate perturbation sanity check (e.g. monkeypatch one input slightly in a throwaway copy) to prove it detects a 1e-8 change. Use .venv/bin/python with PYTHONPATH=python. Report back: the number of cases, total runtime, which public entry points you could NOT cover and why, and any case that behaved nondeterministically (e.g. thread-count dependent results beyond 1e-14 — detect by running compare with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 vs 4 and report the max differences).

The parity battery is built and validated: 128 cases record from the current build and pass against themselves with a largest error of 3e-16. It detects a 1e-8 change. The baseline stays valid after another agent rebuilt the main-tree extension mid-run; details are under Heads-up at the end.

Files (nothing under treams-rs was modified by me):

  • battery.py (single script; modes record, compare, diff, list)
  • baseline.npz (the recording)
  • README.md (how to run it from a worktree, tolerance design, validation results, full case list, what is not covered)

Numbers

  • Cases: 128, recorded as 2793 arrays (about 550k numbers). 793 arrays are pullback gradients. 8 cases deliberately record a ValueError and must keep raising it.
  • Runtime: 25–37 s for the full battery on the original debug extension with 4 CPUs, about 39 s with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. On the rebuilt extension it takes about 7–9 s.

Validation

  • Self-compare, twice: both passed, 0 failing, largest error 3e-16.
  • Perturbation checks:
    • Changing one sphere radius in the diff_cluster inputs by a relative 1e-8, in a throwaway copy, made 2 cases fail at about 2e-8.
    • Scaling outputs by (1 + 1e-8) with a monkeypatch: diff.expansion made 18 cases fail, special.jv 2, and diff.sphere 22.
    • A 1e-12 scaling passed, as intended at rtol 1e-10, and showed up in the report at about 2e-12.
  • Failure modes: a case missing from the battery, a case that newly raises, and a case that no longer raises its recorded exception all report correctly and exit with 1.

Thread-count determinism

  • 1 thread, run twice: bit-identical.
  • 4 threads, run twice: differences up to 6e-16 in hot_scattered_fields_spherical_near_axes, diff_expansion_cylindrical and diff_periodic_conversion.
  • 1 thread vs 4 threads: up to 2.1e-15, in 13 cases: the 8 diff_field_* cases, diff_periodic_conversion, diff_expansion_cylindrical, hot_cluster16_lmax4_fields500, hot_scattered_fields_spherical_near_axes and lattice_expansion_spherical. These are parallel-reduction effects, far below tolerance.
  • Nothing else varied.

Tolerance design

  • Each array must satisfy max|new-ref| <= rtol*max|ref| + atol_scale*case_scale, where case_scale is the largest magnitude in that case. Defaults are rtol 1e-10 and atol_scale 1e-13.
  • 38 special-function arrays (keys ending #ew) are also checked element by element, so tiny Bessel, gamma and large-j Wigner values cannot hide.
  • Integer, boolean and string arrays must match exactly, and NaN/Inf positions must match.
  • The report shows each case's max error and worst key, flags near-misses above 1% of rtol, and lists the 5 largest passing errors.
  • Iterative GMRES solves use rtol 1e-14; iteration counts and residuals are not recorded.

Large-j Wigner 3j

  • The expected change is isolated in 10 wigner3j_large_* cases (j up to 100, extreme m, element-wise checks plus the normalization sum). Check it with --only 'wigner3j_large_*' -v.
  • The current build's normalization for j=100 is off by -1.1e-13, and the j60/45 case contains a noise-level element (about 1e-16 relative). Both will likely change with the fix, which is intended.
  • Translation and lattice kernels that use these coefficients only reach j ≤ 16 in this battery. If the fix moves those small-j values, they will show up in the full compare.

Not covered

  • io.mesh_spheres: gmsh is not installed, and it is not numerical output.
  • support_catalog() / python -m treams_rs: metadata that embeds a source hash, so it changes with every edit.
  • Native functions the public API never calls (_native.lattice_derivatives, lattice_sum, radial, cylindrical, translation, cyl_translation, spherical_wave). A bindings refactor may rightly rename them, so the battery sticks to the public API.
  • Framework adapters are sampled rather than exhaustive. Physical-object gradients are covered for advect, jax and torch, plus a few primitives (advect bessel, lattice_sum and sphere; jax and torch sphere, solve and bessel). jax.wrap, torch.wrap and the remaining advect expert primitives are not called one by one; they wrap the same diff.* records, which are covered directly.
  • ufunc out=/where= plumbing and memory layout are not tested; the battery checks values only.

Heads-up: the main repo changed under the battery

  • At […], after the final baseline was recorded at […], someone rebuilt the main-tree _native*.so. It has uncommitted Cargo.toml changes: a [profile.dev] section with opt-level 1, and opt-level 2 for dependencies. Cargo.lock and crates/treams-core/Cargo.toml (proptest features) are also changed. I did not make these edits.
  • The baseline passes against the rebuilt extension, with differences of at most 4.5e-16. Single-threaded results are bit-identical to the old build. So the baseline is still valid.

Using it from a worktree

  • Run cd <worktree> && PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python .venv/bin/python battery.py compare baseline.npz.
  • The worktree needs its own freshly built python/treams_rs/_native*.so. compare prints which treams_rs path, commit and build profile it imported, so engineers can confirm they tested their own build.
